messages:
devon_procurement: Hey team — WhiteGlove sent over their renewal/commit quote. Need quick eyes on SKU mapping and how the metering shows up on invoices. Link to PDF: https://whiteglove.example/quote/RED-2026. TL;DR: they're proposing 250k token credits/month commit with 10% overage. Thoughts?

maria_finance: can you paste the sample invoice lines? we need to match to our billing parser.

devon_procurement: pasted their sample below (vendor provided):

```
SKU,Description,Units,UnitPrice,Total
WG-TOKENS,Generation tokens,250000,0.0004,100
WG-EMBED,Embeddings units,10000,0.01,100
WG-OVERAGE,Overage tokens,per token,0.0005,
```

sam_product: do they break out by model? our cost attribution needs model-level granularity (e.g., mistral-7b vs redwood-rlhf).

karen_whiteglove: hi all — we can export model-level usage. Default invoice aggregates tokens, but we can enable per-model reporting (additional line item WG-MOD-REPORT $200/mo). sample CSV export snippet below:

```
timestamp,customer_id,model,kind,tokens
2026-02-26T14:03:22Z,redwood_inference,mistral-7b,generation,12345
```

alex_sales: what's the flexibility on the commit cadence? can we do quarterly commits vs monthly?

karen_whiteglove: quarterly prepay is supported. pricing tiers change slightly: 250k/mo commit as monthly = 7% discount; quarterly prepay (equivalent 750k/quarter) bumps to 10% off list.

maria_finance: need to know credit expiry and refund policy for unused tokens. also how proration works on mid-cycle downgrades.

karen_whiteglove: tokens roll over up to 2 months. no cash refunds for early termination by default, but we can negotiate pro-rated credits on a case-by-case basis. proration for downgrades is straightforward — they adjust on the next invoice.

contract-bot: New contract draft uploaded: https://contracts.redwood/whiteglove/drafts/2026-02-26 (version v1.2).

devon_procurement: can we get legal looped? @tess_legal please review the draft and the SKU mapping requirements — we need explicit per-model CSV export and invoice line IDs for our billing pipeline.

tess_legal: I can pick this up tomorrow morning. please tag me on the contract link and highlight any non-standard termination/refund clauses.

sam_product: one more thing — SLA on latency and availability. their docs claim 95th pctl <120ms on p4d for 8k context. do we have bench data or can we run a pilot to verify under real traffic?

karen_whiteglove: we ran an internal sweep on p4d and attached a short report. happy to enable a 2-week pilot with production traffic and enable per-model logging for the pilot. no extra charge for the pilot.

maria_finance: budget modelling question: what's the net effective price if we take an 18-month deal with quarterly prepay + 10% cushion? need to compare to our internal cost targets.

karen_whiteglove: ballpark: effective ~0.00036/token with those terms (includes quarterly prepay discount + volume uplift). I'll put a formal quote together with amortized net pricing and a sample invoice breakdown.

devon_procurement: next steps I propose: 1) legal review (tess), 2) pilot onboarding (sam + karen), 3) finance confirm budget and accounting treatment (maria), 4) vendor to provide per-model CSV export and final quote with invoice line mapping. I'll capture action items in the procurement doc.

tess_legal: noted. will review contract for termination language and data export commitments.

maria_finance: pls cc me once the formal quote and sample invoices are attached. I'll run the numbers against forecast.

alex_sales: +1 on pilot. let's aim to kickoff next week if legal signs off.

karen_whiteglove: thanks all — I'll send updated quote and enable model-level reporting for the pilot. :thumbsup:

devon_procurement: thanks — appreciate quick responses. I'll update the procurement tracker and loop back with dates.
